_meta.description: Sport-specific risk modifiers for return-to-sport decision making. Multipliers adjust base RTS timelines based on the physical demands and injury risk profile of each sport. Sourced from PubMed consensus statements and epidemiological data.
_meta.how_to_use: Multiply base injury timeline by the risk_multiplier for the athlete's sport. A multiplier >1.0 means extended caution is warranted. Multipliers are evidence-informed estimates, not hard rules.

demand_categories.contact: Physical collision with other athletes is part of gameplay
demand_categories.limited_contact: Incidental contact but not central to gameplay
demand_categories.non_contact: No physical contact with other athletes during play

sport_demands: Cutting and pivoting at high velocity
Rapid direction changes on varied surfaces (grass, turf)
rts_specific_tests: 5-10-5 agility drill at full speed
90-minute aerobic endurance test
Sport-specific kicking motion without pain
Heading and aerial contest simulation
GPS match-load simulation: >8km total distance, >600m high-intensity running
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: ACL re-injury in soccer: graft rupture 10%, contralateral 8% at 5 years. Males ≤18 have 44% further ACL injury risk (PMID 36190172). Italian Consensus recommends GPS criteria for RTP (PMID 31673400).

sport_risk_modifiers.sport: Australian Rules Football (AFL) / Rugby League / Rugby Union
rts_specific_tests: Collision simulation testing
Maximal sprint series: 10×40m
Match simulation at full contact level
Shoulder stability under load (rugby / AFL marking)
GPS: match-load threshold >10km, >800m high-speed running
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: High hamstring recurrence risk in sprint-dominant field sports. Contact risk elevates concussion danger. All concussion RTS requires stepwise protocol minimum (PMID 30356457).

sport_demands: High ankle-loading on hard court surfaces
Jump-shot mechanics with patellar tendon high load
rts_specific_tests: Drop jump landing symmetry
SEBT or Y-balance for ankle stability
VISA-P score ≥80 for patellar tendinopathy
Sport-specific jump-shot and lay-up sequence without pain
3-on-3 non-contact session before full 5-on-5
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Patellar tendinopathy (Jumper's Knee) is the leading chronic basketball injury; load management is essential for prevention. Hard court surfaces increase ankle sprain frequency.

sport_demands: Repetitive cyclic loading (thousands of foot strikes per session)
Eccentric hamstring and calf loading at high velocities
Training load errors most common mechanism of injury
Female runners at higher RED-S/stress fracture risk
rts_specific_tests: Pain-free progressive running program (5km → 10km → race pace)
Calf raise endurance ≥90% contralateral
Single-leg hop for distance LSI ≥90%
Running mechanics analysis (no antalgic pattern)
Training load: <10% weekly increase rule
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Stress fractures high-risk locations (navicular, femoral neck, anterior tibial cortex) require imaging clearance before running resumes (PMID 9421865). Female athletes with menstrual disturbance at elevated bone stress risk.

sport_demands: High-velocity overhead throwing mechanics (≥80mph in pitchers)
Repetitive eccentric shoulder load at deceleration
Shoulder ER/IR ratio critical for injury prevention
rts_specific_tests: Functional Throwing Performance Index (FTPI) ≥80%
Closed kinetic chain upper extremity test
Upper quarter Y-balance symmetric
Staged throwing program (15 → 30 → 45 → 60 → 90 feet → game distance → game intensity)
Shoulder strength ER:IR ratio within 15% of contralateral
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Rotator cuff repairs in overhead athletes require the most conservative timelines (9–12 months for throwers) due to high eccentric deceleration forces (PMID 37588949).

sport_demands: Early sport specialization increases RED-S/stress fracture risk
rts_specific_tests: Bilateral landing mechanics without valgus or spinal flexion
Pain-free gymnastics vault or beam elements
Bone density screening if RED-S suspected
Sport-specific skills testing under coaching observation
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Gymnastics/cheerleading athletes at high risk for low bone density and stress fractures due to energy restriction. RED-S screening mandatory before RTS in young athletes.

sport_demands: Pool used as rehab modality for many injuries
rts_specific_tests: Pain-free freestyle and backstroke at training pace
Shoulder impingement tests negative
Timed swim sets at race pace
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Swimming can be used therapeutically during Phases 1–2 for non-shoulder injuries. Shoulder injuries in swimmers may require extended rotator cuff rehabilitation due to volume demands.

sport_demands: Non-weight-bearing cyclic knee and ankle loading
High cadence repetitive patellar tendon stress
Bike fit critical for injury prevention
Used as cardiovascular rehabilitation tool for many injuries
rts_specific_tests: Pain-free cycling at race intensity and duration
VISA-P ≥80 if patellar tendinopathy
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Cycling is frequently used as Phase 1–2 rehabilitation tool for lower limb injuries. Cycling RTS after PATELLAR_TENDINOPATHY or ACHILLES requires load monitoring.

sport_demands: Highest concussion incidence of all team sports
rts_specific_tests: Full-contact practice clearance by team physician
Concussion clearance per stepwise protocol minimum
Helmet-contact simulation before return
Sport-specific positional testing (QB throwing, lineman blocking)
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: NFL PCL injuries have RTS <6–12 months (PMID 41811648). Concussion protocol mandatory under US federal and state laws. Highest single-sport concussion incidence.

sport_demands: Overhead serving with high rotator cuff demands
Explosive lateral movement on clay, hard court, grass
High volume of unilateral upper limb use
rts_specific_tests: Pain-free serving mechanics at full speed
Lateral movement agility (T-test, 4-corner drill)
Shoulder strength ER:IR ratio within 15% of contralateral
Baseline rally simulation at match intensity
sport_risk_modifiers.notes: Serving demands can be highest force requirement in upper limb sports – rotator cuff healing must be complete before aggressive serving resumes.
